text:
Sophie (ACME): Hey team, hitting an issue with the rerank endpoint. We call /v1/rerank with model id `rerank_v0.9` and getting back `model_not_found`. Also when I tried the fallback model the scores are all 1.0 — suspicious.

Jordan (Support): Sorry to hear that — can you paste the curl you used and a snippet of the response? Also which account/org id?

Sophie (ACME): Org: acme-42

curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "rerank_v0.9", "query": "best antivirus", "candidates": ["A","B","C"]}'

Response:
```
{"error":{"code":"model_not_found","message":"model id 'rerank_v0.9' not found"}}
```

Jordan (Support): Thanks. Looks like that model id was deprecated last quarter. Sorry we didn't bubble that up earlier. We're checking whether there's an alias mapping for compatibility. @Luca any pointers on expected score schema differences between v0.9 and current rerank models?

Luca (ML Eng): quick summary: older rerank_v0.9 returned normalized scores in [0,1]. Current rerank-* models emit raw logits by default (can be positive/negative). If a client assumes 0..1 and interprets logits as probabilities, you can see weird all-equal scores after post-processing. We added an optional query param `normalize_scores=true` to restore old behavior. Also note model ids were consolidated under aliases like `rerank-stable` — the direct legacy id was removed from the catalog.

Priya (SRE): From infra logs for acme-42 around 2026-03-14T12:04:10Z:
```
2026-03-14T12:04:10Z ERROR router: lookup_failed model_id=rerank_v0.9 tenant=acme-42
2026-03-14T12:04:10Z WARN fallback: routed_to=rerank-stable note="compatibility fallback"
```
The router did a fallback, but the score transform step on the client side wasn't applied (client assumes normalized). 

Jordan (Support): Sophie, two options to get you unstuck now:
1) Change model to `rerank-stable` and include `"normalize_scores": true` in the request body. Example:
```
{"model":"rerank-stable","query":"best antivirus","candidates":["A","B","C"],"normalize_scores":true}
```
2) If you must keep `rerank_v0.9` in your code path, we can create a temporary alias mapping for your org to route `rerank_v0.9` -> `rerank-stable` and enable legacy normalization server-side. This requires an infra change and approval.

Sophie (ACME): Option 1 worked — switching to `rerank-stable` + `normalize_scores` returns expected numbers like 0.87 / 0.12 / 0.01. Thanks! Can we get a heads-up next time a model id gets removed?

Jordan (Support): Totally agreed. I'll open an escalation to Product to add earlier deprecation notices to the console and to email org admins for affected model ids. @Luca can you add a note to the model catalog docs about `normalize_scores` and aliasing behavior?

Luca (ML Eng): On it — will add doc and a small compatibility FAQ. Also proposed short-term fix: Server will accept legacy model tag for 30 days for orgs that recently used it. Priya, can infra add a TTL'd alias mapping for acme-42?

Priya (SRE): I can provision a TTL alias; will need a change request. Jordan — can you file a support-change for acme-42 with requested TTL (30d)?

Jordan (Support): Filed CHG-8931 for acme-42 to add alias `rerank_v0.9` -> `rerank-stable` for 30d. Deploy-bot status:

deploy-bot: CHG-8931 created and queued for approval :white_check_mark:

Sophie (ACME): Appreciate the quick turnaround. Leaving this open until docs/notifications are in place.

Jordan (Support): Leaving thread open. Follow-ups: doc PR, console deprecation banner, email to admins. Closing note when done. :thumbsup:
